ig_poc:
The busiest price on yesterday's ES chart is a level worth marking today.

Volume profile shows how many contracts traded at each price, stacked sideways instead of under each bar. The tallest row is the point of control: the price where the most business got done.

How I read it: I treat the point of control as the market's idea of fair value. When price holds away from it, one side is in control. When price drifts back to it, the market is balancing, and I expect chop there, not a clean run.

Put it on your chart before the session, then let price show you what it does at that level.

Save this post and pull it up the next time you mark levels.

fb_news:
Some of the fastest ES moves of the week are on the calendar days in advance.

Scheduled economic reports, like inflation data, the jobs report and Fed announcements, can push ES several points in a few seconds. In that burst, liquidity thins out, and a stop order can fill well past the price you set.

None of that has to be a surprise. Before your session, check the economic calendar for anything due during the hours you trade. If a big release lands inside your window, decide ahead of time: stay flat into it, or be in with a stop you can live with even if it slips.

The calendar belongs in your risk plan, right next to your stop.
